items.title: Simple interest
items.content: For principal \(P\), annual rate \(r\%\), time \(t\) years: \(SI=Prt/100\); amount \(A=P+SI\).

items.title: Compound interest
items.content: Annual compounding: \(A=P(1+r/100)^t\), \(CI=A-P\). For half-yearly compounding, rate per period is \(r/2\)% and number of periods \(2t\), if the quoted rate is nominal annual.

items.title: Time and rate units
items.content: Match time to the rate period. Convert months to years for annual rates unless compounding period is specified. State currency and rounding.

items.title: Exam checks
items.content:
Write the rate as a percentage and divide by 100 exactly once.
For compound interest, distinguish amount from interest.

items.title: Principal, rate, time and amount
items.content: Principal is initial money; interest is the increase; amount is principal plus interest. Worked example: ₹5,000 at 6% simple interest for 2 years gives \(SI=5000\cdot6\cdot2/100=₹600\), amount ₹5,600.

items.title: Simple interest over time
items.content: SI grows by the same amount each equal period because it is calculated on original principal. Worked example: ₹8,000 at 5% for 9 months: \(8000\cdot5\cdot(9/12)/100=₹300\).

items.title: Compound interest
items.content: Interest is added to the balance before the next period. Worked example: ₹10,000 at 10% annually for 2 years gives amount \(10000(1.1)^2=₹12,100\), so CI = ₹2,100.

items.title: Find an unknown quantity
items.content: Rearrange the interest formula. Worked example: ₹400 SI on ₹2,000 for 4 years means annual rate \(r=100(400)/(2000\cdot4)=5\%\).

items.title: Compare SI and CI
items.content: For the same positive principal, rate, and whole-year term, annual CI exceeds SI after the first year because later interest earns interest. Worked example: ₹1,000 at 10% for 2 years: SI ₹200; CI ₹210.

items.title: Compounding frequency
items.content: More frequent compounding changes the number and size of periods. Worked example: ₹1,000 at nominal 12% for one year compounded monthly gives \(1000(1.01)^{12}\approx₹1,126.83\).

items.title: Calculate SI and amount
items.content: Worked example: ₹12,000 at 7% for 18 months: \(t=1.5\); SI = ₹1,260; amount = ₹13,260.

items.title: Calculate compound amount
items.content: Worked example: ₹4,000 at 5% annually for 2 years: \(A=4000(1.05)^2=₹4,410\), CI ₹410.

items.title: Find time or rate
items.content: Rearrange \(SI=Prt/100\), keeping the same time unit as the rate. Worked example: ₹240 SI on ₹2,000 for 3 years gives r = 100·240/(2000·3) = 4%.

items.title: Compare investments
items.content: Use equal principal, annual rate, time and compounding convention before comparing totals. Worked example: ₹1,000 at 10% for 2 years gives SI amount ₹1,200 and annual CI amount ₹1,210.

items.title: Reverse amount question
items.content: Worked example: ₹1,210 is the amount after 2 years at 10% CI. Principal is \(1210/(1.1)^2=₹1,000\).

items.title: Derive simple interest
items.content: One year’s interest is \(Pr/100\). Over \(t\) years without compounding, multiply by \(t\): \(SI=Prt/100\).

items.title: Derive compound amount
items.content: After one period balance is \(P(1+r/100)\). Applying the same growth factor for \(t\) periods gives \(A=P(1+r/100)^t\).

items.title: Difference for two years
items.content: For annual compounding, year one interest is \(Pr/100\); year two also earns interest on that first interest. The extra compound interest over SI is \(P(r/100)^2\) for two years.

sections.title: Common errors and how to avoid them

items.title: Using amount as principal
items.content: Interest formulas use the original principal for SI; the amount is the final balance.

items.title: Month/year mismatch
items.content: Convert months to a fraction of a year or use the stated period convention.

items.title: Applying CI for a partial convention
items.content: Follow the stated compounding schedule and do not assume annual compounding when another frequency is specified.

items.title: Rounding each period
items.content: Keep full precision through compounding; round the final currency amount only.

keyTakeaways: SI is calculated on original principal.
CI earns interest on accumulated interest.
Time must match the rate and compounding period.
